idiom_name: static `XxxMother` class in the test project
implementation_notes: The usual .NET realization is a static test-source class - 'internal static class CustomerMother { public static Customer Vip(string name = "Ada") => new Customer(...); }' - or a TestData helper class of expression-bodied factory methods; xUnit offers constructor/IClassFixture setup for per-class fixtures but nothing for cross-class canned objects. Records with required/init members shorten the hand-written case, and when only validity matters, generator libraries (Bogus Faker<T>, AutoFixture) fill object graphs with far less code; keep the hand-written mother for named business examples that tests read and assert against.
pitfalls: A static factory that caches and returns the same instance gives every test the same mutable graph; construct a fresh object (or deep-clone) per call.

Object initializers and reflection-based fillers bypass constructor validation, so the mother can hand out objects that production code could never create - route creation through the real constructor when invariants exist.
Generator output is arbitrary: tests that assert on generated values need a fixed Randomizer.Seed, otherwise they fail intermittently.
Static mutable counters (id sequences) inside the mother are shared across the whole test process and race under parallel xUnit collections.
